correctness.rationale: Complete bitmask enumeration gives 5,828 faces, exact augmented mod-two boundary ranks (1,19,141,519,991,921,315,5), only four mod-two classes in degree five, and reduced Euler characteristic -4, forcing precisely four rational classes in that degree. Exhaustive graph-automorphism enumeration yields 120 elements and a central antipode; independent signed-Lefschetz and orbit-graph traces coincide for all 120. Character comparison exactly identifies the twisted five-cube augmentation module; both full-group and rotation-restricted norms equal one, proving absolute irreducibility. Rational quotient invariants follow from admissible barycentric subdivision and characteristic-zero averaging. All claims have exact scope; the integral lattice and quotient torsion are not asserted.

originality.rationale: The previously published same-complex theorem identifies only the ordinary wedge homotopy type and four-dimensional Betti number; it does not imply the action on rational homology. The classical five-cube permutation representation likewise does not imply which topological representation appears or that inversion acts as minus identity. Barmak and Berghoff do not cover the object-action-parameter claim. Exact published-finding corpus indexed queries and targeted public-literature searches produced no covering implication; publication-priority certainty is not claimed.

value.rationale: The natural five inscribed cubes carry a concrete five-point A5 permutation action, while the independence complex has four-dimensional rational fifth homology. Identifying the action as its antipodally twisted augmentation explains an absolutely irreducible module rather than only the known Betti number. The cube-stabilizer quotient has a nonzero rational top class, but inversion removes it and makes the full group and rotation quotients rationally acyclic; this structurally motivated contrast is invisible to nonequivariant homotopy.
